page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-96 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the g4 server family. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture and 360.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 3.75 GB per vCPU.

The instance is equipped with two NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture family, providing a combined total of 192 GB of GPU VRAM. This server does not include any local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage. Additionally, the instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Given the high density of dedicated compute cores and dual professional-grade GPUs, this instance represents a specialized hardware class designed for resource-intensive workloads. The lack of local storage and public IPv4 addresses are architectural tradeoffs to consider when planning deployments. Appropriate workloads for this configuration include GPU-accelerated rendering, 3D visualization, machine learning inference, and data science tasks requiring significant graphics processing power and dedicated CPU resources.
